sovereign_country.strategic_role: 连接拉美市场的欧洲商贸桥梁、本地化仓配与数字游民签证

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Manufacture of Autonomous Crop Spraying Unmanned Aerial Vehicles

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–U.S. Tax Convention for the Avoidance of Double Taxation (1990)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, approving the AML/CFT Regulations; Real Decreto-ley 7/2021, de 27 de abril, transposing Directive (EU) 2018/843 (AMLD5); Royal Decree 179/2019, de 22 de marzo, regulating the Registro de Titularidades Reales (UBO Register); and Ley de Sociedades de Capital (Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010).

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of legal identification (passport or national identity document) of each shareholder and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent national authority or issuing authority of the shareholder's country of origin

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing (Certificado de Vigencia) of any non-resident corporate shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Commercial registry or company registrar in the shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Consular Legalization (if non-Hague party)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney granted to the Spanish attorney/notary for incorporation formalities
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Foreign public notary or competent authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter from the shareholder's or UBO's financial institution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Bank or financial institution in the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Consular Legalization or Apostille (when signed before a notary)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory PEP screening is conducted at initiation and on a risk-sensitive basis thereafter, in accordance with Spanish AML/CFT Law. All UBOs, shareholders and directors must be screened against the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Sanctions List, OFAC SDN List (for USD transactions), and domestic PEP and adverse information registries maintained by SEPBLAC (Servicio Ejecutivo de la Comisión de Prevención del Blanqueo de Capitales) and the AEAT (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria). Enhanced due diligence applies where any PEP link, high-risk third country, or adverse media finding is identified.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (Sede Electrónica, www.rmercaentral.es) and the CIRCE platform (www.circe.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be stated in Spanish or transliterated into Latin characters; the name must be written in Spanish script, including accents and punctuation, and must not be identical or phonetically similar to any existing name in the Registro Mercantil Central. The chosen denomination must be followed by the sufix 'Sociedad Limitada' or 'S.L.' (or 'S.L.U.' for unipersonal). The application complies with Articles 401-403 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital and the Implementing Regulations of the Commercial Registry.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the Registro Mercantil Central issues a negative certification explaining the grounds. The applicant may file a recurso de alzada (administrative appeal) before the Dirección General de los Registros y del Notariado (DGRN) within one month of notification, or a recurso de reposición before the RMC itself. The appeal must attach the negative certificate, the proposed alternative names, and the applicant's identification documents. Alternatively, a new name certificate can be requested without prejudice to the appeal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible beyond provisional domiciliation; the manufacture of agricultural drone sprayers requires a physical registered office, technical installations and, under AESA (State Aviation Safety Agency) licensing, a maintenance/technical facility in Spanish territory. A virtual office may only be used temporarily until the physical site is fully operational.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (≥90% within the first 12 months) for the manufacturing facility and registered office; the industry carries a high-risk classification driven by dual-use technology, export reporting obligations, and AML/CFT scrutiny.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Application for negative name certificate (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
Notarial incorporation deed (Escritura de Constitución) preparation and notarization
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff based on share capital

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Commercial registry filing fee (Registro Mercantil de la provincia del domicilio)
AML/UBO due-diligence and PEP/sanctions screening (external provider)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Approved external advisory firm or SEPBLAC-recognized provider

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarization, apostille and sworn translation of foreign corporate documents
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Foreign notarial offices, competent authority for apostille, and sworn translator (traductor jurado)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal advisory and pre-incorporation due diligence retainer

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Royal Legislative Decree 1/2010 of 2 July, approving the consolidated text of the Spanish Companies Act (Ley de Sociedades de Capital), particularly Articles 4, 20, 21, 22, 23, 31, 32, 33, 40, 210, and 233; Royal Decree 1784/1996 on the Mercantile Registry; and Law 14/2013 on support for entrepreneurs, as amended.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: The Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil) for the province of the company's registered office, under the Directorate-General for Legal Security and Public Faith (Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública). Incorporation deeds are authorized by a Spanish notary.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Public deed of incorporation (escritura pública de constitución), filed for registration with the competent provincial Mercantile Registry.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: An SL may be formed with share capital of EUR 1 or more. Capital contributions must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation. While capital is below EUR 3,000, statutory safeguards apply: at least 20% of annual profit must be allocated to legal reserve until capital plus reserve reaches EUR 3,000, and, on liquidation with insufficient assets, shareholders may be jointly liable for the shortfall up to EUR 3,000. No general statutory escrow account is required. Non-cash contributions require a description and valuation in the deed; founder liability rules apply.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the Company accepts the subscriptions and payments for the shares set out in the incorporation deed and confirms that the subscribed capital has been fully paid. RESOLVED, that the registered office be established at [full address], Spain, subject to registration and any required premises approvals. RESOLVED, that [name] is appointed [sole director/joint director], and [name] is appointed [secretary/other officer, if applicable], with the powers and term provided in the bylaws and applicable law. RESOLVED, that the director is authorized to obtain the Company’s tax identification number, complete registration and tax filings, open bank accounts, and apply for required activity, industrial, environmental, and product-compliance authorizations.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Central Mercantile Registry (Registro Mercantil Central), through its official online name-reservation service
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for a negative certification of the proposed company name. The certificate must identify the intended founders or applicant and remain valid for execution and registration within its statutory validity period. Provide alternative names to reduce rejection risk.
required_dossiers: Proposed company names in order of preference
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is unavailable or confusingly similar to a registered name, submit alternative names and obtain a fresh negative certification before signing the deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish notary selected by the founders; CIRCE/PAE may be used for eligible standardized formations
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Set the registered office, corporate purpose, share capital, share allocations, management structure, and fiscal year. Use a corporate purpose covering manufacture and commercialization of agricultural drones and related equipment, subject to applicable licensing. Confirm that the proposed activity codes and scope are accurate.
required_dossiers: Founder identities and, for legal-person founders, current registry evidence and representative authority
NIE or NIF details for foreign founders and directors, as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct inconsistencies in the corporate purpose, governance provisions, names, addresses, or capital schedule before notarial execution; obtain translations and apostilles or legalization for foreign documents where required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: All founders, or duly empowered representatives, execute the public deed. The notary verifies identity, capacity, name certification, bylaws, capital subscription, and payment evidence. Cash contributions may be evidenced by a bank certificate or, where legally permitted, by founders’ responsibility statements in the deed. Foreign powers and corporate documents must satisfy Spanish legalization, apostille, and sworn-translation requirements when applicable.
required_dossiers: Evidence of cash contributions or deed statements permitted by law
Non-cash asset descriptions and valuation information, if applicable
Foreign corporate authorizations, powers of attorney, apostilles/legalization, and sworn translations, if applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Provide missing evidence, correct the deed through a notarial rectification or supplementary deed, and re-execute any required signatures.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain provisional tax identification and complete tax formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish State Tax Agency (Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, AEAT), through its electronic office or the relevant tax office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply for the company’s NIF using Form 036 and submit the incorporation deed and identification documents. File the regional Tax on Property Transfers and Documented Legal Acts declaration, normally Form 600, where required; incorporation is generally exempt from payment, but filing formalities may remain applicable under regional practice. Confirm the applicable regional procedure.
required_dossiers: Form 600 or applicable regional declaration and exemption basis, if required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to AEAT or regional tax-office requests with corrected forms, deed extracts, authority evidence, and clarification of the exemption or tax position.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the SL with the provincial Mercantile Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Mercantile Registry for the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the notarial deed, required tax filings, and NIF information for registration. The notary may transmit the deed electronically. Registration gives the company legal personality as an SL. Obtain the registry inscription data and request the definitive NIF from AEAT if a provisional NIF was issued.
required_dossiers: Negative name certification, where not already electronically verified
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Cure registry defects within the notice period by submitting corrected documents or a supplementary notarial deed; seek reconsideration or appeal under applicable registry rules if a defect is disputed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Complete tax, beneficial-ownership, and employer registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: AEAT; Mercantile Registry; and Spanish Social Security General Treasury (Tesorería General de la Seguridad Social), as applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File or update Form 036 for commencement and tax census details before commencing taxable activity. Record and report beneficial ownership under applicable Spanish and EU rules. Register as an employer and obtain a contribution account code before hiring employees; register directors or workers in the correct Social Security regime based on their role and control.
required_dossiers: Director and employee identity and Social Security details
Workplace and payroll information, if hiring
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Correct census, beneficial-owner, or Social Security filings promptly and provide supporting ownership, employment, and control documentation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Secure premises and local activity approvals before operations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipality (Ayuntamiento) where the facility is located; autonomous-community industrial and environmental authorities where applicable
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Before fitting out or operating the manufacturing site, confirm zoning compatibility and determine whether the activity requires a prior municipal license, responsible declaration, environmental instrument, construction permit, or industrial-facility registration. Submit facility plans and technical reports under the relevant municipality and autonomous-community procedures.
required_dossiers: Site plans and technical project signed by qualified professionals where required
Activity description, equipment, process, and capacity information
Fire, accessibility, environmental, and workplace-risk documentation as locally required
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Address zoning or technical deficiencies, revise the project, and obtain written clarification from the municipality or competent regional authority before construction or operation.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: No single national industrial licensing board applies. The competent authority is the autonomous community’s industrial-safety department for industrial-facility registration and applicable product-market surveillance, together with the municipality for premises and activity approvals. AESA (Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Aérea) regulates relevant UAS operations, not general drone manufacture.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No single Spain-wide manufacturing operating permit title. Depending on the site and process, the required authorization may be a municipal activity or environmental license, or a responsible declaration, together with registration of applicable industrial facilities in the autonomous community. Determine the exact instrument from the facility location, processes, capacity, and emissions.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: The competent environmental authority of the relevant autonomous community; the Ministry for the Ecological Transition and the Demographic Challenge (Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico) is competent for specified state-level cases.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: No automatic EIA classification follows solely from manufacturing agricultural drones. Screening under Law 21/2013 on Environmental Assessment and regional rules is project- and location-specific. Most assembly-only facilities may require no EIA, but may still require a municipal environmental instrument; listed projects or significant impacts may require simplified or ordinary environmental assessment.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: There is no universal drone-manufacturing numeric threshold. Obtain any required discharge authorization from the competent basin authority or sewer operator and comply with permit-specific limits, applicable industrial-emissions rules, air-quality requirements, and hazardous-waste obligations under Law 7/2022. Classify and manage solvents, coatings, batteries, oils, and contaminated materials through authorized waste channels. Agricultural pesticide spraying is subject to separate plant-protection-product and UAS operating restrictions; manufacturing authorization does not authorize spraying.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Comply with applicable municipal fire-prevention and building approvals, the Spanish Building Code, workplace risk-prevention requirements under Law 31/1995, and applicable industrial-safety regulations. Fire-service review or certification, structural/load checks, and commissioning inspections depend on the premises, equipment, and regional/local rules. Obtain any required construction, occupancy, activity, and industrial-facility approvals before use.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – Central Electronic Portal: sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A non-resident foreign entity engaged in taxable operations in Spain must obtain a Spanish Tax Identification Number (NIF) for legal persons, format N + 8 digits. The procedure is: (1) appoint a tax representative if the entity is not established in the EU/EEA and no reciprocity exemption applies; (2) execute a power of attorney in favour of the representative or legal counsel; (3) file Form 036 (Declaración censal) electronically through the AEAT portal or by paper at the competent local tax office, accompanied by certified incorporation documents, the foreign tax identification certificate or VAT registration evidence, and the appointment of the Spanish representative where required; (4) receive the provisional NIF, subject to validation; (5) after AEAT verification, obtain the definitive NIF and, if making taxable supplies, the Spanish VAT registration number. Entities established in the EU may instead use the VIES exchange mechanism and are registered under their EU VAT ID plus the Spanish intra-EEA operator code where applicable.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Spain does not operate a US-style check-the-box regime; an Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada (SL) is a per-se corporation taxable at entity level under Impuesto sobre Sociedades. Available elective mechanisms relevant to the tax profile include: (a) the elective consolidation regime for groups of companies under Article 58 et seq. of Ley 27/2014 (at least 75% direct or indirect ownership for 1 year); (b) the reduced 15% corporate income tax rate for newly created SLs engaged in an economic activity during the first two taxable years if the entity opts for that special regime and meets the filing conditions; (c) intercompany allocation and Spanish permanent establishment closing agreements; (d) no hybrid or anti-hybrid 'elections' are available—ATAD transposition rules (Articles 15 bis through 15 nonies Ley 27/2014) apply mandatorily to deny mismatches.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido (IVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: There is no general turnover-based registration threshold for established businesses; any entrepreneur or professional carrying out taxable supplies is required to register and become a taxable person from the first transaction. For non-established EU vendors making distance sales of goods into Spain, the applicable EU-wide annual distance-selling threshold is EUR 10,000, above which Spanish VAT becomes due and SPAIN VAT registration is required. Non-EU foreign vendors have no registration threshold and must register from the first taxable supply in Spain, subject to reverse charge mechanisms on certain B2B supplies.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spain imposes phased mandatory B2B electronic invoicing under Ley 18/2022 ('Crea y Crece'), requiring interoperable electronic invoices in structured format for all commercial transactions between private businesses once the implementing regulation is fully effective. In parallel, the AEAT real-time system 'Suministro Inmediato de Información' (SII) applies to large taxpayers with annual invoicing above EUR 6,000,000 and to entities in certain regimes, requiring transmission of invoice records to AEAT's web services/API within 4 days of invoicing. The Verifactu regime under Ley Antifraude (Ley 11/2021) obliges all billing software to produce authentic, complete, integral, legible and traceable invoice records ('Registro de Facturación') and to make those records electronically available to AEAT upon request. There is no separate mandatory digital stamp or pre-clearance of individual invoices for the standard SL exporter, but the combination of SII, Verifactu and upcoming Crea y Crece interoperability constitutes the real-time clearance framework.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods to non-EU destinations qualify for 0% VAT under Article 21 of the Spanish VAT Law when the goods are physically dispatched or transported out of the EU by the seller, by the customer, or on behalf of either party, and the seller has in its possession within the statutory timeframe an accepted customs export declaration (DUA) evidencing departure from EU customs territory. For supplies related to agricultural drone equipment, the same zero-rating applies provided the drones are actually shipped outside the EU; installation, commissioning, remote support and related offshore services supplied to a non-EU business customer are generally zero-rated or outside the scope of Spanish VAT if the reverse charge applies, subject to the place-of-supply rules. The exporter must retain transport documents, payment evidence and the customs exit confirmation (passed to the 'E-AD' or CMR / B/L / AWB records) to demonstrate the principal condition: the goods left Spain within 90 days of dispatch.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DUA – Documento Único Administrativo) showing the accepted 'Salida de la UE' customs status
Export accompanying document (EAD) or customs warehouse release confirmation
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, CMR or equivalent transport document proving physical departure from EU territory
Commercial invoice issued by the exporting SL
Packing list and, where relevant, certificate of origin or movement certificate EUR.1
Bank SWIFT / TT wire credit or Inward Remittance Certificate evidencing receipt of export consideration
Payment guarantee or letter of credit instruments if payment is deferred, plus correspondence evidencing the payment schedule
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export zero-rating claims are subject to strict AEAT audit scrutiny. Acceptance of a DUA with subsequent non-departure, fictitious exports, manipulated transport documents, or failure to produce credible proof of dispatch within the 90-day rule will trigger adjustment of the zero-rated supply to 21% VAT, with late-payment interest and input VAT clawback. Under Ley 58/2003 General Tributaria, an incorrect application of the zero rate is a taxable 'regularisation' attracting surcharges (recargos del periodo ejecutivo) of 5% to 20%, and in cases of negligence or intent, proportional penalties of 50% to 150% of the amount. False documentation supporting an export claim may be treated as tax fraud, carrying potential criminal liability under the Spanish Criminal Code and, where customs value or export licenses for dual-use or security-sensitive goods are involved, sanctions under Spanish customs and export-control law. Forensic cross-checks through the AEAT computer systems, maritime manifest databases, and banking payment records are routine; failure to receive export proceeds within the 180-day documentary benchmark increases the presumption of artificiality and invites retrospective clawback.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España — Central Bank of Spain, operating within the European System of Central Banks; external financial affairs and foreign-investment oversight also involve the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation and the Commercial and Foreign Investment Registry under the Secretary General for Investment and Foreign Trade
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain is a full convertibility jurisdiction under the euro area legal framework. Both current account transactions (goods, services, royalties, dividends, profit remittances) and capital account movements are generally unrestricted under Articles 63–66 TFEU and Spanish Act 19/2003 on Foreign Investment. The euro is freely convertible; there are no domestic exchange controls, quantitative limits, or prior administrative FX licensing requirements. Profit and dividend remittance to non-residents is permitted without exchange-control authorization, but is subject to substantive tax requirements including the non-resident income tax withholding (currently 19% for outbound dividends, plus possible treaty relief) and Bank of Spain statistical reporting. A strategic foreign-investment screening regime under Law 7/2020 and Royal Decree 571/2020 applies to non-EU/EFTA investors acquiring Spanish targets in critical sectors (dual-use, critical technologies, security, strategically sensitive physical or digital infrastructure). For an AgTech drone sprayer with ISIC 2821 production and potential dual-use UAV classification, the screening threshold should be assessed at the very early stage: if non-EEA ownership exceeds the statutory thresholds (10% or direct control, or 5% in regulated strategic areas), prior authorization may be required; otherwise, an ex-post declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry suffices. Capital reparations and inward equity investments require no central bank permit, but the funds must reach a Spanish bank account and be reported through the balance-of-payments declaration framework.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under EU law and Spanish legislation there is no mandatory export-proceeds surrender ratio, no forced conversion timeline, and no requirement that export receipts be repatriated to Spain within a fixed period. The exporting SL may retain hard-currency proceeds in resident accounts, use them directly for foreign debt service or inputs, or convert them to EUR at freely negotiated bank rates. However, intermediaries must report all cross-border transactions to the Banco de España balance-of-payments statistics in accordance with Bank of Spain Circular 4/2004, with individualized reporting for transactions equal to or exceeding EUR 50,000 (or the prevailing updated threshold). For documentary compliance, the exporter must maintain the customs export declaration (DUA), the commercial invoice, transport documents (airway bill, bill of lading), and, for UAV-related products, the relevant dual-use/export-control end-user certificate or authorization under EU Regulation 2021/821. The statutory no-surrender treatment does not exempt the SL from providing full supporting evidence to the receiving bank upon conversion of foreign currency into EUR, nor does it waive tax documentation for export income.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium for a well-regulated EEA-licensed EMI that can operate in Spain under PSD2 passporting, and Low for non-EEA offshore EMIs. A Spanish SL can maintain a virtual IBAN, receive trade payments, and settle operational costs through an EMI, provided the EMI holds a valid payment institution licence under Directive (EU) 2015/2366 and is registered in Spain through the Bank of Spain passport register. However, offshore digital EMIs (e.g., chartered in a non-EEA jurisdiction without an EU branch) are not permitted to hold Spanish-resident local nostro accounts or issue Spanish IBANs unless they establish a locally authorized branch or agent bank. The main legal constraints are: AML obligations under Act 10/2010, the prohibition on unlicensed payment activity, the need for segregated client accounts, and the practical reluctance of tier-1 Spanish banks to accept an offshore EMI as a counterparty for high-value AgTech export settlements. In consequence, the preferred route is to open a primary treasury account at a tier-1 Spanish bank and use an EEA-licensed EMI only for collection of payments from overseas B2B customers or disbursement of small trade expenses.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Spanish AML regulation (Act 10/2010, as amended) does not impose a general statutory mandate that directors must appear personally at a bank branch. Remote account opening is permitted where the bank has implemented an AML-compliant video-identity verification process, uses qualified electronic signatures, and verifies identity documents in real time under the EU AML standard. In practice, tier-1 Spanish commercial banks classify the AgTech drone sector as a high-risk customer and will in most cases require at least one physical interview with the ultimate beneficial owner(s), a senior director, or a locally appointed representative with a notarized power of attorney. CaixaBank and BBVA generally permit a hybrid process: the legal representative appears in Spain for a face-to-face compliance interview, and the other directors undergo remote video KYC. Banco Santander often requires the local representative to be present at branch for the opening and for the release of any capital escrow. For a wholly remote structure without any physical trigger, onboarding viability decreases significantly. The use of a Spanish lawyer or a corporate services provider as an authorized signatory does not eliminate the need to validate the beneficial owner's identity; it merely shifts the interview obligation if the bank approves a PoA mandate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Industry classification as manufacturing of unmanned aerial systems (UAS/drones) with dual-use and export-control implications
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Comprehensive documentation package: (1) EU Dual-Use Regulation 2021/821 effective authorization or written exemption confirmation from the Spanish Secretary of State for Trade; (2) product specification sheets evidencing the non-weaponisable agricultural spraying design, spraying flow rates, battery capacity, and military-spec limitation strategies; (3) end-user certificate from each agtech customer; (4) corporate export-control manual with internal compliance program, screening logs, and denial-list checks; (5) copy of the SL's ISO 9001 quality or CE/ENAC certifications; (6) independent trade counsel legal opinion classifying the product as EAR99/ITAR-free comparable dual-use low-tier if relevant; (7) patents and utility model filings showing agritech purpose.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Complex or non-EU Ultimate Beneficial Ownership (UBO) structure, including trust, offshore holding, or non-resident shareholders in the drone manufacturing entity
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier containing notarized and apostilled incorporation deed (escritura pública) of the Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada; current Registro Mercantil certificate; completed UBO register filing (RDL 7/2021 and EU Directive 2015/849) with passport and tax residence certificate of each UBO; full corporate chain chart from legal counsel; statutory balance sheet and bank reference detail; sworn declarations of source of wealth and source of funds; third-party compliance due-diligence report; certification that no politically exposed person (PEP) is involved or, if so, a PEP declaration and enhanced-compliance plan.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Planned inbound capital injection from non-EU jurisdiction exceeding EUR 250,000 without a previous banking relationship
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: The SL must provide: (a) signed investment or shareholders agreement covering the capital increase; (b) notarized board resolution approving the injection; (c) source-of-funds evidence such as audited financial statements of the investor for the last three years, bank account statements for the preceding twelve months, and tax-residence certificate of the investing entity; (d) confirmation of the origin of wealth from the remitting bank; (e) a sworn certificate from the accounting auditor tracing this specific injection to declared corporate profits or documented asset disposal; (f) foreign investment registry filing confirmation (ex-post declaration path); (g) escrow agreement signed with the receiving Spanish bank to ensure traceability of funds from the source bank account to the SL's corporate capital account.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payments through high-risk jurisdictions or trade counterparties involving agrochemical inputs or agricultural customers without robust sanctions screening
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Evidence bundle comprising: commercial invoices and contracts with final beneficial flow; customs export/import declarations; phytosanitary certificates for agricultural inputs; safety data sheets for any agrochemical substances; OFAC and EU Consolidated List screening result reports generated by a reputable compliance database; an end-user certificate from each counterparty; transport documents including bill of lading or airway bill with full cargo description; corporate cross-border payment policy demonstrating compliance with international sanctions; written certification that payments will not involve U-turn transactions or trans-shipment to sanctioned entities; and a duty-of-care report under the OECD Guidelines for Multinational Enterprises.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a non-EEA or offshore digital EMI for collection of export proceeds, triggering heightened correspondent banking risk
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Defense package: copy of the EMI's payment institution licence or digital-bank charter from its home regulator; proof of Spain passporting/agent registration under PSD2; EMT/EMI audited financial statement for the previous year; client-money segregation confirmation from an independent auditor; monthly reconciliation of all receipts and outgoing payments to the governing Spanish treasury account; board-approved treasury policy stating that the EMI is a secondary collection channel only; Spanish-counsel legal opinion on the EMI's capacity to hold funds and the enforceability of customer agreements; and AML/KYC data-sharing agreement in compliance with GDPR and Act 10/2010.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocol for inbound capital injection into the SL: (1) Before transfer, the SL opens a EUR-denominated Capital Escrow Account at a tier-1 Spanish bank and executes an escrow agreement confirming the intended use (equity subscription or capital contribution). (2) The foreign investor instructs its bank to send an SWIFT MT103 using the SL's IBAN and the payment reference 'CAPITAL INCREASE' and Spanish balance-of-payments purpose code '601 – Inward direct investment' or '603' for non-resident capital contributions; field 70 must contain the investment registration number where applicable. (3) The sending bank must transmit the underlying investment agreement and evidence of regulatory/screening clearance if the investor is non-EU/EEA, to enable automatic credit via the correspondent account at the receiving Spanish bank. (4) The Spanish bank will verify the source of funds, conduct UBO and sanctions screening, and release the amount into the operational account after the notary deed of capital increase is filed at the Registro Mercantil. (5) The SL must submit the corresponding post-closing foreign-investment declaration to the Foreign Investment Registry of the Ministry of Economy within the statutory filing window (typically one month after execution); no prior central-bank FX permit is required for euro transfers. (6) All fees should be charged to the sending side using 'OUR' billing to preserve traceability and avoid reduction in the reported capital amount. If the capital is in USD or a non-euro currency, a sub-account or a treasury conversion arrangement with a recognized bank must be used, and the resulting EUR amount must match the corporate records.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: The primary clearing rails for outbound trade disbursements are: (a) SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) for EUR payments to EEA suppliers, utilities, and European sub-distributors; (b) SWIFT MT103 direct telegraphic-transfer for immediate TT settlement in USD, GBP, or other convertible currencies, using the correspondent network of the Spanish bank; and (c) Commercial Documentary Letters of Credit (MT700/MT710) for large AgTech drone export contracts, with the SL as beneficiary and a Spanish bank as advising/confirming bank to mitigate non-payment and country risk. For USD disbursements to Latin American counterparties, the bank routes via US Fedwire/CHIPS through a New York correspondent; for transactions with China-related suppliers, the SL may use a standard MT103 with CNY offshore settlement (CNH) or the Commercial LC denominated in CNY, provided the bank has CNY clearing capabilities. The SL must include the correct ISO 20022 purpose code on each disbursement—typically 'TRDC' for trade, 'PDPE' for payment employment? or more practically the Spanish purpose code '010' for export/import trade settlements—and must attach pro-forma invoices, contracts, customs declarations, and the applicable export/import license. For cash management, the SL should operate an EUR operational account as the master treasury account and one USD or multi-currency settlement account; any excess FX exposure is systematically hedged through the treasury policy rather than left open. Incoterms and documentary requirements should match the settlement rail chosen, with a preference for LC payment terms on orders above a EUR 250,000 threshold.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: EUR/USD and EUR/GBP outright foreign exchange forward contracts (plain vanilla, flexible and window forwards) transacted with a Spanish credit institution under ISDA/EMTA documentation
EUR/foreign-currency FX swap transactions for short-term liquidity management and rollover of export receivables
Cross-currency interest-rate swaps (CCIRS) to hedge the currency and interest-rate risk of the initial capital injection or long-term foreign-currency debt

Non-deliverable forward (NDF) contracts involving non-convertible or restricted currencies (e.g., Argentine peso, offshore CNY) executed through the Spanish bank's international NDF desk, subject to internal limit approval
Over-the-counter EUR/USD and EUR/Latin-American-currency collar structures (zero-cost collars, participating forwards) to cap hedging cost while retaining partial currency upside
Exchange-traded futures options and currency futures on Eurex or CME, permitted under the SL's investment-policy threshold when the counterparty clearing exposure is within the treasury risk mandate
FX options and exotic forward-based structures (accumulators/deccumulators) only where pre-approved by the bank's risk committee and the SL's board as part of a documented treasury hedging policy

Risk participation agreements and trade finance interest-rate/currency facilities embedded in commercial export credit arrangements, authorized under Spanish banking regulations if the SL maintains qualified-investor status for the trade amount

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: 4 months after fiscal year end (e.g. 30 April if year-end 31 December)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines up to €300,000; risk of company dissolution after two years of non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month of any ownership change or by 30 April if no changes
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fines €300–€1,500 per omission; additional administrative sanctions possible

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory independent audit if company exceeds two of the following: net turnover > €2 million, total assets > €1 million, or average number of employees > 50
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Spanish General Accounting Plan (PGC) for small entities; IFRS for larger or listed companies

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Annual review and update of Ultimate Beneficial Owner information in the public Registro Mercantil register; notify changes within one month

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: 0-500 USD (home office permitted; professional agent services typically 100-400 USD annually)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: 0 (if exempt) to 2,000-6,000 USD (typical fee for mandatory audits)
